BUSINESS · business GUIDE

Business Loan — Apply & Eligibility Guide

• Last updated: 2026-09-15 · 3 min read
Share:
In simple words:

A business loan provides funding for working capital, equipment, expansion or other business needs. Eligibility, interest and repayment depend on the lender, product and borrower profile.

S
Samjho Content Team ✓

Trusted and policy experts simplifying MSME, tax, and compliance for India. Verified by Chartered Accountants.

Simple explanation

Business loans may be term loans, working-capital facilities, cash credit, equipment finance or government-linked products. Choose based on what the money is for and how the business will repay it.

Lenders usually review business vintage, turnover, banking history, credit profile, income, existing obligations, KYC and business records. MUDRA products are designed for eligible micro enterprises under their applicable categories and rules.

Compare total cost, not only the advertised interest rate. Check processing fees, collateral, prepayment terms, repayment schedule and the Key Facts Statement or equivalent documents.

Why does it matter?

Borrowing can help a healthy business grow, but an unaffordable EMI can damage cash flow and credit history. A simple projection of monthly sales, expenses and repayment is essential.

Example

In numbers

Before applying for a ₹3 lakh working-capital loan, a shop owner can list monthly cash inflow, fixed costs, supplier payments and an EMI buffer, then compare bank and eligible MUDRA routes.

Types and eligibility

Common options include term loans for a fixed purpose, working-capital facilities for operating cash flow, equipment finance and micro-enterprise products. Eligibility differs by lender and may include minimum turnover, vintage, credit score, banking records and repayment capacity.

Documents and interest rates

Typical documents can include PAN, Aadhaar or other KYC, bank statements, GST or tax records where applicable, business proof, financial statements, address proof and a project report. Rates may be fixed or floating and depend on risk, product and lender; ask for the complete cost in writing.

Apply online

Apply through a bank's official website or branch, or through the official route for an eligible MUDRA product. Compare offers, verify the lender, read the sanction and loan documents, and never share OTPs or pay an unknown agent.

Advertisement

Important things to know

  • Match loan tenure to the business cash-flow cycle.
  • Check the total repayment and all fees before accepting.
  • A government-linked product still has eligibility and lender appraisal.
  • Keep EMI payments on time to protect the business credit profile.

Common mistakes

  • Choosing based only on a low headline interest rate.
  • Borrowing without a cash-flow plan.
  • Sharing sensitive credentials with unverified loan agents.
  • Ignoring late fees, collateral or prepayment conditions.

Frequently asked questions

What is a business loan used for?

It can fund working capital, equipment, stock, expansion or other approved business purposes, depending on the product.

Who is eligible?

Eligibility varies, but lenders commonly assess business history, turnover, documents, credit profile and repayment capacity.

What documents are needed?

KYC, bank statements, business proof, tax or GST records where applicable, financial information and a project or use-of-funds note may be requested.

What is a MUDRA loan?

MUDRA supports eligible micro-enterprise lending through participating lenders under current product categories and guidelines.

How are interest rates decided?

The lender considers product, borrower risk, business profile, tenure and market or policy conditions. Ask for the complete cost.

Can I apply online?

Yes, use the official bank or lender website and verify the lender before sharing information or paying fees.
